3_current_alternative.strongest_alternative: Lithium battery (finite life, 5-8 years, requires replacement surgery)
3_current_alternative.why_inadequate: Actual cardiac harvesting in target implant location. Whether 10 μW is achievable in shunt geometry.

6_remaining_uncertainty.primary_uncertainty: Actual cardiac harvesting in target implant location. Whether 10 μW is achievable in shunt geometry.
known_failures: Arrhythmia model (70% reduction) more aggressive than published (10-30%)

7_validation_investment.experiment: Physical energy harvesting test: build harvesting circuit (cardiac motion + buffer), implant in mock cardiac environment, measure power output over 30 days. Compare to 99.9% uptime model.
7_validation_investment.success_threshold: Sustained power output >= 5 μW for 30 days (sufficient for pacemaker-grade operation). Uptime >= 95%.
7_validation_investment.t2_conversion_path: Current T1 → $$5-10K physical test experiment → T2-CONDITIONAL

8_strategic_buyer_fit.ideal_buyer: Medical device OEM with implantable power management pipeline (Medtronic, Boston Scientific)
8_strategic_buyer_fit.strategic_reason: Hybrid power (harvesting + buffer) eliminates battery replacement for ultra-low-power implants. Platform technology.
8_strategic_buyer_fit.capabilities_required: Energy harvesting, power management IC, implantable device manufacturing
8_strategic_buyer_fit.why_this_buyer_would_care: Battery-free implantable sensors are a new product category. 99.9% uptime is the key metric.

10_why_now: Battery-free implantable sensors are a new product category. Energy harvesting has matured. Medical device companies face battery replacement costs ($45K/surgery). Hybrid power eliminates this for low-power implants.
